title: viola canina subsp. jordanii
intro: Viola canina subsp. jordanii, commonly known as Jordan's violet or wild violet, is a subspecies of perennial flowering plant in the violet family. This plant has been traditionally used to treat various health issues, including colds, fever, and gastrointestinal problems, due to its health benefits such as anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antiviral properties. The therapeutic actions of Viola canina subsp. jordanii include its ability to reduce fever, alleviate respiratory issues, and soothe digestive problems. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, glycosides, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
